en: Itivuttaka 63: Tikanipāta, Dutiyavagga (The Second Chapter) Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard: "Monks, there are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world. What three? The person who is like a lotus flower, the person who is like a jasmine flower, and the person who is like a blue lotus flower. And how, monks, is one a person like a lotus flower? Here, monks, a certain person dwells with his mind overcome by sensual lust, burning with sensual lust; yet he does not utter the words: 'I am one whose mind is overcome by sensual lust, burning with sensual lust. Just as a lotus flower, though born in the water and grown in the water, rises up above the water and stands unsoiled by the water—so too, monks, is one a person like a lotus flower. And how, monks, is one a person like a jasmine flower? Here, monks, a certain person dwells with his mind overcome by ill will, burning with ill will; yet he does not utter the words: 'I am one whose mind is overcome by ill will, burning with ill will. Just as a jasmine flower, though born on the earth and grown on the earth, rises up above the earth and stands unsoiled by the earth—so too, monks, is one a person like a jasmine flower. And how, monks, is one a person like a blue lotus flower? Here, monks, a certain person dwells with his mind overcome by anger and resentment, burning with anger and resentment; yet he does not utter the words: 'I am one whose mind is overcome by anger and resentment, burning with anger and resentment. Just as a blue lotus flower, though born in the water and grown in the water, rises up above the water and stands unsoiled by the water—so too, monks, is one a person like a blue lotus flower. These, monks, are the three kinds of persons found existing in the world. Thus it was said by the Blessed One. Having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and entered his dwelling. Then, soon after the Blessed One had departed, a certain bhikkhu approached the Venerable Ānanda and said to him: "Friend Ānanda, the Blessed One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling while delivering a brief teaching. It would be good, friend Ānanda, if you could explain the meaning of this in detail. "It is fitting for you, friend, to ask the Blessed One himself about the meaning of this. As the Blessed One explains it to you, so you should remember it. "But, friend, the Blessed One has risen very early; he will be weary. Perhaps later on, when the Blessed One is at ease, you might approach him and ask about the meaning of this. As the Blessed One explains it to you, so you should remember it. Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and reported to the Blessed One the entire conversation that had taken place between him and that bhikkhu. "So it is, Ānanda! So it is, Ānanda! There are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world. What three? The person who is like a lotus flower, the person who is like a jasmine flower, and the person who is like a blue lotus flower. And how, Ānanda, is one a person like a lotus flower? Here, Ānanda, a certain person dwells with his mind overcome by sensual lust, burning with sensual lust; yet he does not utter the words: 'I am one whose mind is overcome by sensual lust, burning with sensual lust.

Just as a lotus flower, though born in the water and grown in the water, rises up above the water and stands unsoiled by the water—so too, Ānanda, is one a person like a lotus flower. And how, Ānanda, is one a person like a jasmine flower? Here, Ānanda, a certain person dwells with his mind overcome by ill will, burning with ill will; yet he does not utter the words: 'I am one whose mind is overcome by ill will, burning with ill will. Just as a jasmine flower, though born on the earth and grown on the earth, rises up above the earth and stands unsoiled by the earth—so too, Ānanda, is one a person like a jasmine flower. And how, Ānanda, is one a person like a blue lotus flower? Here, Ānanda, a certain person dwells with his mind overcome by anger and resentment, burning with anger and resentment; yet he does not utter the words: 'I am one whose mind is overcome by anger and resentment, burning with anger and resentment. Just as a blue lotus flower, though born in the water and grown in the water, rises up above the water and stands unsoiled by the water—so too, Ānanda, is one a person like a blue lotus flower. These, Ānanda, are the three kinds of persons found existing in the world. Thus spoke the Blessed One. Having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and entered his dwelling. Then, soon after the Blessed One had departed, the Venerable Ānanda addressed the bhikkhus: "Friends, bhikkhus! "Yes, friend," those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Ānanda. The Venerable Ānanda said this: "Friends, the Blessed One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling while delivering a brief teaching. It would be good, friends, if we were to go to the Blessed One and ask him about the meaning of this. As the Blessed One explains it to us, so we should remember it. "Yes, friend," those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Ānanda. Then the Venerable Ānanda and those bhikkhus approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. The Venerable Ānanda reported to the Blessed One the entire conversation that had taken place between him and those bhikkhus. "So it is, Ānanda! So it is, Ānanda! There are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world. What three? The person who is like a lotus flower, the person who is like a jasmine flower, and the person who is like a blue lotus flower. [The Blessed One then repeated the entire discourse as above. These, Ānanda, are the three kinds of persons found existing in the world. Thus spoke the Blessed One. Delighted, those bhikkhus rejoiced in the words of the Blessed One. *** Itivuttaka 63: Tikanipāta, Dutiyavagga (The Second Chapter) Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard: "Monks, there are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world. The Discourse on Time-Spans.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:
“Bhikkhus, there are these three time-spans.”
“What are the three?
The past time, the future time, and the present time—
these, monks, are the three times.”
The Blessed One spoke this matter.
Regarding this, it is said:
“Beings who perceive what can be described,”
Established in that which can be expressed,
and not fully understanding what can be expressed,
they go to the yoke of death.
Having fully understood that which can be expressed,
one does not conceive of an expresser;
touched by liberation through the mind—
The unsurpassed state of peace.
He is indeed perfected in what can be expressed,
being peaceful and delighting in the state of peace.
“Having investigated and practiced, established in the Dhamma, the one who has attained knowledge does not come within the range of reckoning.
This matter was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The fourth.
